text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it actually does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the furniture stays in the same place logically, but everything becomes easier to find and use. The main goal is to boost readability, making the code simpler for others (and your future self) to understand. This often involves breaking large functions into smaller ones, renaming unclear variables, or removing duplicate lines. Over time, skipping refactoring leads to technical debt—the hidden cost of messy code that slows down new features and makes bugs harder to fix. A little regular cleanup saves a lot of headache later.
